timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Rate limiting. Sounds like a speed bump.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: It's a bouncer, a firebreak, and a cost control all in one.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Credential stuffing, scraping, DDoS — and one buggy client eating all capacity.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Token bucket, fixed window, sliding window, leaky bucket. Each trades simplicity for accuracy.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Limits need shared state, like Redis. One instance alone can't enforce a global limit.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After. Well-behaved clients back off politely.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Throttling sheds load by delaying or dropping work to keep a steady pace.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: By identity, IP, or key. And tune it so legitimate spikes aren't blocked.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So it's both defense and availability?
